# SYMBOLS.md — exported-symbol parity (Phase A / Phase D)

Derived mechanically from `nm -D --defined-only` on both shared libraries.

* **C reference `.so`** — `cc -shared -fPIC c_src/src/main.c c_src/src/inventory.c
  -Ic_src/include -o libdriver_c.so` (`c_src/CMakeLists.txt` builds those same two
  translation units; it just links them as an executable, so the shared-library
  form is built with the identical sources/flags plus `-shared -fPIC`).
  Built automatically by `build.rs` into `$OUT_DIR/libdriver_c.so`.
* **Rust `.so`** — `target/<profile>/libdriver.so`, from `crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]`.

Reproduce with:

```sh
./run_all.sh            # builds both and diffs the symbol sets
# or manually:
nm -D --defined-only $(ls target/debug/build/driver-*/out/libdriver_c.so | head -1) | awk '{print $3}' | sort > /tmp/c.txt
nm -D --defined-only target/debug/libdriver.so                                     | awk '{print $3}' | sort > /tmp/r.txt
comm -23 /tmp/c.txt /tmp/r.txt   # symbols missing from Rust  -> must be empty
comm -13 /tmp/c.txt /tmp/r.txt   # symbols only in Rust       -> must be empty
```

## Result

| metric | value |
|--------|-------|
| symbols defined by C `.so` | **63** |
| symbols defined by Rust `.so` | **63** |
| C symbols missing from Rust `.so` | **0** |
| extra non-C symbols exported by Rust `.so` | **0** |
| undefined non-libc symbols in Rust `.so` | **0** (only `libc`/`libgcc`/`ld` imports; see below) |

Undefined symbols in the C `.so` are all libc: `__isoc99_sscanf`, `fgets`, `free`,
`malloc`, `printf`, `putchar`, `puts`, `realloc`, `stdin`, `strcmp`, `strncpy`
(plus the weak `__gmon_start__`, `__cxa_finalize`, `_ITM_*` stubs every ELF gets).
The Rust `.so` imports the same allocator/IO primitives (`malloc`, `realloc`,
`free`, `write`, `read`, …) from libc, plus the usual `pthread_*`/`dl*`
dependencies of Rust's `std`; nothing from the C translation unit is left
undefined.

## Every C symbol, its origin, and whether the Rust `.so` exports it

All 63 are `T` (global text) in both libraries. The `array_*` / `list_*` names are
generated by the `DEFINE_ARRAY(TYPE)` / `DEFINE_LIST(TYPE)` macros in
`generic_containers.h`, instantiated for `int`, `double`, `item_t` and `order_t`
by `inventory.c`; the Rust side generates them with the `define_array!` /
`define_list!` macros in `src/capi.rs`, so the macro-generated names exist there
too.

## Notes on individual symbols

* `main` — `main.c` is part of the shared library, so the C `.so` exports `main`.
  The Rust `cdylib` exports it from `src/capi.rs` (`#[no_mangle] pub unsafe
  extern "C" fn main() -> c_int`, delegating to `demos::c_main`). It is excluded
  only under `cfg(test)`, where the unit-test harness provides its own `main`;
  the shipped `cdylib` always has it (verified by `nm`). The `driver` executable
  does **not** link the library crate — it compiles the same modules directly and
  supplies a normal Rust `fn main` — so there is no duplicate-`main` link error.
* `find_expensive_items` — declared in `inventory.h` and defined in
  `inventory.c`, but never called from `main.c`. It is exported by both `.so`s and
  is covered by the differential tests (`tests/inventory_funcs.rs`,
  `tests/errors.rs`) even though no demo exercises it.
* `array_*_get` — no bounds or NULL check in C; the Rust translation performs the
  same unchecked raw read so that in-bounds behaviour (including reading elements
  that are still present after `clear`) matches byte for byte.
* Struct-by-value ABI: `print_item(item_t)`, `print_order(order_t)`,
  `create_item(...) -> item_t`, `create_order(...) -> order_t` pass/return
  `item_t` (120 bytes) and `order_t` (80 bytes) by value. The Rust `#[repr(C)]`
  definitions reproduce the C layout exactly, verified against the C compiler:

  | type | size | align | field offsets |
  |------|------|-------|---------------|
  | `item_t` | 120 | 8 | `id` 0, `name` 4, `category` 68, `price` 104, `quantity` 112 |
  | `order_t` | 80 | 8 | `customer_id` 0, `customer_name` 4, `total_amount` 72 |
  | `array_TYPE_t` | 24 | 8 | `data` 0, `size` 8, `capacity` 16 |
  | `list_TYPE_t` | 24 | 8 | `head` 0, `tail` 8, `size` 16 |
  | `list_node_int_t` | 16 | 8 | `data` 0, `next` 8 |
  | `list_node_item_t_t` | 128 | 8 | `data` 0, `next` 120 |
  | `list_node_order_t_t` | 88 | 8 | `data` 0, `next` 80 |

  Because the Rust containers also allocate through the same libc
  `malloc`/`realloc`/`free`, a container created by one library is byte-identical
  to one created by the other; the tests exploit this by handing C-built
  containers to Rust entry points and vice versa.

## Parity is also enforced by the test suite

`tests/symbols.rs` runs `nm -D --defined-only` on both libraries during
`cargo test` and asserts:

* `rust_so_exports_every_c_symbol` — the difference in both directions is empty,
  and every one of the 63 names resolves through `dlsym` in *both* libraries;
* `rust_so_has_no_unexpected_undefined_symbols` — nothing that belongs to the
  translated C code is left as an import in the Rust `.so`;
* `documented_symbol_set_is_complete` — both libraries' symbol sets equal the
  exact set documented above (4 element types × 6 array ops + 4 × 6 list ops +
  8 `inventory.c` functions + 6 `main.c` functions + `main` = 63).

All 63 symbols are additionally *called* by the differential tests:
`ArrayApi`/`ListApi` bind the 48 macro-generated names for all four
instantiations, `InventoryApi` the 8 `inventory.c` entry points, `DemoApi` the 6
`main.c` display functions, and `driver_e2e::main_symbol_scenarios` calls the
exported `main` of each `.so` in a forked child.

## Note on the release build

`[profile.release] panic = "abort"` makes cargo build the library twice during
`cargo test --release` (once with `panic=abort` for the `cdylib`, once with
`panic=unwind` for the test harness), which produces cargo's benign
"output filename collision" warning for `deps/libdriver.so`. The artifact the
tests load is the uplifted `target/release/libdriver.so` produced by
`cargo build --release`, i.e. the `panic=abort` `cdylib`; `run_all.sh` builds it
before running the tests and re-checks its symbol table each time.
